known_charts.regularity: A rank-ten, minimally two-periodic standard AS window with a reduced twenty-point scheme realizes two distinct simultaneous Veronese embeddings and is genuinely singly symmetric. Four normal quadratic parameters, a polynomial-module basis lift, quadratic nullhomotopies and depth prove all-degree exactness from a conditional degree-six test.
known_charts.current_result: Complete classification of the three-axis companion family. Regularity is equivalent to Delta=sum(a_i^2 a_j^2) nonzero; the rank-ten torus gives a two-dimensional image and exactly two active axes give bisymmetric rank eight. Every unmarked indexed isomorphism class is specified by the unordered projective triple of coefficient squares, including the positive-dimensional point-scheme boundary.

For Klein-graded singly symmetric windows with regular character spaces, having a simple fixed point forces the bisymmetric or the three-axis chart. If a character of H is absent, every regular window belongs to those charts or a two-plane-pair PBW chart, with an effective decision on all inputs. A rank-ten PBW example has skew point lines, outside the entire three-axis chart. Profile (3,1,1,1) forces full symmetry in AS.

The complete (2,2,1,1) Klein class of standard AS windows is covered by the bisymmetric chart and the closure of the single four-dimensional second-completion family. Singular cross blocks force bisymmetry for every AS tensor, including every thin zero pattern, and are effectively decided. All unequal completions with invertible cross blocks, even exceptional fibers or vanishing thin coefficients, lie in the same irreducible closure.
known_charts.rational_regular_input: The explicit rational matrices used for the twenty-point configuration are standard AS of minimal period four, with four central quartic parameters. See thm:klein-rational-period-four.
known_charts.generic_isomorphism: Four rational coefficients modulo at most sixteen character reindexings; the three projective point configurations have automorphism group Klein four and are mutually inequivalent. See sections/klein_generic_isomorphisms.tex.
known_charts.center_lift: On the rational two-dimensional slice v=4,w=6, the generic periodic quartic center has five generators as a vector space (character dimensions 3,2,0,0). A single Zariski-open neighborhood of the certified rational chart point b=2,c=3 consists entirely of standard regular closed fibers finite free of rank 256 per start over four central quartics. A finite constructible rank test recognizes this certificate on the whole second-completion closure.
known_charts.generic_center_and_PI: Over four algebraically independent second-completion parameters, the periodic quartic center has dimensions (3,2,0,0). One dense open containing the original rational point consists entirely of AS closed fibers finite free over four central quartics. Every standard AS point anywhere in this closure satisfies the uniform standard identity s_512.

known_charts.current_result: The full nondegenerate Klein (2,2,1,1) rank chart, including all coefficient-zero determinant fibers, is covered by the elliptic closure and the four exceptional presentations. If both determinant quadratics vanish identically the normalized base has eight explicit types, each with one bilinear equation for the entire fiber; all lie in the elliptic closure.
known_charts.unmarked_character_frames: The thin pencil and the branch divisor of the recovered quartic select a unique unmarked character frame at both full-rank samples and on their neighborhoods. Standard windows on this open are index-preservingly isomorphic exactly when one of 32 monomial permutations passes an integral torus test, including coefficient zeroes.
known_charts.quintic_defect: On both signed fixed elliptic curves at every ordinary characteristic-zero slope, the geometric support of the length-five defect equals that of the length-four defect. It consists of the twelve old sections and the four positive opposite-determinant sections, with the four negative pairs coincident when lambda squared times z equals minus one.

known_charts.current_result: With no Klein grading imposed, the singly symmetric rank-ten locus is smooth at the rational regular sample and has a fourteen-dimensional unmarked family, geometrically generically AS, with trivial projective indexed stabilizer and minimal period four. At this and the rank-sixteen sample the unrestricted normal tangents have dimensions (5,2,4,4) by character and all primary obstructions vanish. The extra alternating direction maps the opposite kernel isomorphically to its cokernel.

The zero-pairing boundary contains an entire non-AS bilinear curve at (z,lambda)=(3,2), with generic degree-six path dimensions (92,84,85,84), and a non-AS two-parameter sublocus x=z-1 with degree-four dimensions (35,36,36,35).

configuration_projection.result: The generic recovery degree from one projected configuration is exactly two. The two finite-edge AS windows are the original orientation and its reversal; one ordered first edge determines the extension. At both rational samples the same classification holds. A pencil of quartics with twenty triple points recovers every normalized square root, including the exclusion of degenerate Grassmann candidates.

known_charts.current_result: The intrinsic rank-three marked Ore criterion works also for positive-dimensional edges. For a smooth elliptic ternary point graph the mark is unique. Outside translations of orders two and four, the correction space vanishes except for the inversion linear part, where it has dimension two for every admissible curve. All these positive-edge windows have period one.

For a plane-graph ternary base the marked correction space is the fifteen-dimensional Euler quotient for the identity, zero for nonidentity without a fixed line, and the three binary quadratics with scalar shift for a fixed line. All have period one. For all nonidentity plane-graph bases the unmarked classes are determined by projective conjugacy in the no-line case, or by the multiplier up to inversion, the quadratic rank and the incidence with the center of a transvection. All transvection classes are flat limits of homologies.

Every ordinary positive fixed rank-fifteen window on y=lambda*x^3 is standard Koszul and two-sided AS-regular and is free of rank 256 per start over four central quartics when lambda lies in a number field with a place above three of residue degree at most two. This holds for the full eight residual tubes, at every geometric horizontal coordinate. The indexed invariant curve of this pencil has genus two except at lambda=1/27; the shift quotient has genus one and the reduced exceptional curve is rational with exactly two period-one classes.

Every ordinary positive fixed rank-fifteen window has a common four-center cut with a central monomial basis through degree nine at all starts. The ninth uncut and cut dimensions are 220 and 20. An upper bound of five for one odd-length character is enough: Walsh translations act transitively on the characters and preserve the zero-character center, so four open Grassmannian conditions intersect. A signed bivariate descent and eleven finite exceptional fibers verify the bound on the whole ordinary locus.

When the five-center quotient vanishes in length eight, its normal words through seven give a single lifted arrow table for every four-center direction. Quadratic residuals on those words determine every higher quotient exactly. On the ordinary Hilbert stratum all central-direction minors through thirteen have degree at most 21. The two-variable residue-field quotient by columns two through five has the full target profile through thirteen at start zero with an explicit localization at 171 irreducible pivot factors.

Every ordinary positive fixed rank-fifteen window is standard quadratic Koszul and two-sided AS-regular, free of rank 256 per start over four common central quartics. The signed sextic curve and all 100 remaining closed orbits on it and three off it are certified. Including the four formal boundary points, indexed classes form the surface y != 0, p^2=x^3-27y, q^2=(1-x)^2-4y. Exactly two points have least period one and the others have period two.

For tensors admitting the specified Walsh symmetry bases, the two adjacent rank-six conditions reduce to signed row and column sums of a three-by-three matrix of squares after excluding exponential growth. Every opposite-rank-fifteen candidate is exactly a normalized regular Pauli window. Opposite ranks eleven and thirteen are impossible for standard objects. At ranks twelve and fourteen three nonzero blocks on each side are necessary and sufficient for regularity. Rank twelve has one quantum class; rank fourteen includes a single additional orbit of normalized presentations at H squared equal to four, certified by four-start central cuts.
known_charts.all_parameters_AS: An adjacent-rank-six Walsh tensor is standard quadratic Koszul two-sided AS-regular exactly when three colors survive on each cut and the signed three-by-three square matrix N has rank two. Every rank-one point has at least 36 paths of length four. At every rank-two point, sparse cases included, the transfer of the missing words is an orientation-reversing split-quaternion isometry. It supplies four normal quadratics whose central squares give freeness of rank 256 per start.

known_charts.unmarked: Finite incidence plus marked isomorphism test for all, and unique mark over every integral cubic graph.

No centrality, normality or right-module finiteness of the parameters is needed. The finite test itself certifies finiteness, freeness and both AS conditions on success.

known_charts.scope: At least one smooth quadric graph and point fibers at all four projections in each direction.
known_charts.current_result: When all edge projections have zero-dimensional fibers and any one edge is a smooth quadric graph, all edges are compatible quadric graphs. The entire standard branch is an affine line minus one point with parameter m squared plus inverse m squared. Clifford traces prove regularity exactly away from the two excluded values m=plus or minus one, all indexed periods are one, and every class is polystable, has no quantum orbit limit and has no regular normal linear sequence.

All standard windows admitting a compatible quotient onto a smooth commutative quadric are classified, including additional lines and nonreduced point schemes. Two invertible two-by-two spin blocks give the complete list, with two curves meeting at one point, the scalar class and two Jordan types. Every finite-Frobenius candidate on this branch is regular of period one. With zero-dimensional edge projection fibers, any proper surface factor has total degree at most two.

All standard windows admitting an integral quadric cone quotient are classified by a dual-number spin matrix: three scalar-leading cases, a projective conjugacy family, and one alternating trace-zero case. All have exact period one and only the alternating case has the bare cone as its entire point graph. Every plane component with point projection fibers supplies a regular normal linear sequence. This covers every surface component in the finite-projection branch by a smooth quadric quotient, a cone quotient, or a normal linear plane quotient.

All standard windows with a regular normal linear plane quotient are classified by explicit special-value forms for every projective Jordan type, including the nonsemisimple cases and ordinary Lie central extensions. At most two plane marks occur outside the commutative point; factoring three quadrics and recomputing the alternate normal form completely decides unmarked isomorphism. Together with the two quadric classifications this exhausts the entire surface case with zero-dimensional projection fibers.

For every finite-Frobenius point graph with one-dimensional image and point projection fibers, the total curve degree is at most seven including multiplicities. The third Picard difference vanishes and the degree of each component is constant across positions. The unique smooth elliptic quartic, when present, has second difference killed by twelve. A disjoint isolated residual to a smooth curve has length 18-4d+2g.

For a one-dimensional point graph containing a smooth elliptic quartic and with point projection fibers, regularity is equivalent to an invertible two-by-two tensor in the quartic product kernel of the two quadratic section ideals at each position. Every accepted algebra is free on both sides over the induced two-variable polynomial-type indexed subalgebra. The entire branch admits a finite atlas of pairs of six-planes in eight-space over elliptic polarization data, with a finite residual group and period tests.

A finite-Frobenius point graph window with three coherently commuting letters is automatically Koszul and AS regular and free on both sides over their polynomial algebra. Any graph of maximal degree seven is a pure genus-five curve. In the smooth integral case it is exactly the alternating kernel window of two canonical projections at an ordered pair differing by exact four-torsion. Finite Frobenius and graph tests suffice, with isomorphism by curve isomorphisms of the ordered pair and period one exactly when the two points can be exchanged. Nonemptiness of its parameter locus is not asserted.

All smooth septic point graphs with point fibers are explicitly classified by eight coefficients of three canonical quadrics, subject only to smooth complete intersection. The residual action is a three-dimensional effective torus and a swap. All are bielliptic, their isomorphism classes have dimension five, generic period two, and all period-one specializations are decided by changing the sign of the mixed coefficient and testing that action. Two smooth examples and their full finite Frobenius ranks are checked.

For any finite orbit of genus-one quartic complete-intersection subcurves of a one-dimensional point graph, including nonreduced marks, regularity is equivalent to invertible quartic product relations between consecutive permuted marks. This covers every reduced quartic complete-intersection mark, even when distinct marks share components; all marks are then enumerable and unmarked isomorphism and periods reduce to the finite list of comparisons.

Across positive-dimensional fibers as well as point graphs, the mixed-endpoint four-step determinantal correspondence has only simple cycles in every finite strongly connected subsystem, with at most four consecutive cyclic components. Every recurrent irreducible sequence of dominant correspondences is birational in both directions and has generic return multiplicity one. Different dominant returns of matched lengths agree at every intermediate point.

For any point-fiber window, a cubic slice with all three supports of dimension three produces a ternary subalgebra over which the window is left and right free. Regularity is equivalent to rank-one avoidance in its three ternary nets. For all finite four-edge Frobenius candidates the quadratic relation spaces automatically avoid rank one, by length-ten planar residuals. Consequently opposite rank below six is empty and every finite candidate of opposite rank six or seven is standard AS, with previously finite indexed isomorphism and period tests.

For every finite four-edge Frobenius window of every opposite rank, the canonical four-step map on its length-twenty point scheme is the identity including all nilpotents. Each fixed closed point gives a nonzero three-by-three determinantal cubic separating the opposite local socle. At a reduced mark both opposite contractions are invertible between their three supports, and every relation uniquely removes a mixed point-coordinate letter.

At any reduced point of a finite Frobenius point graph, the entire four-tensor has a canonical traceless presentation by four triples of three-by-three matrices. Both adjacent rank-six conditions reduce to one commutator equation linear in two of the triples. All marked basis changes, the opposite rank and the common-plane condition at rank eight are explicit. The complete kernel of point evaluation has a three-letter presentation by eight cubic commutators per position, with no higher defining relations.

On every invariant smooth nondegenerate curve component the opposite two-point contraction has a finite flat rank-drop divisor of bidegree (2,2), with class the diagonal plus the inverse four-step graph twisted by the inverse polarization second difference on both factors. Small fixed loci force zero second difference in genus at least two; the bielliptic exceptional divisor and all elliptic translation cases are explicit. Elliptic quartic second differences are six-torsion. On every smooth septic the canonical four-step map is the bielliptic deck involution and the divisor is the nonzero two-torsion displacement on its elliptic quotient.

No finite-Frobenius window has point graph a smooth nonhyperelliptic sextic of genus three with point projection fibers. The determinantal cubic forces its length-two rank drop onto a trisecant, yielding a fixed-point-free automorphism and a Jacobian identity. These force the Fermat plane quartic and one of thirty polarization sequences. Exact good reduction bounds every cubic overlap by two.

A finite Frobenius candidate with all four point correspondences graphs cannot have point scheme the disjoint union of a smooth integral sextic and a finite scheme. In the remaining hyperelliptic genus-three case two ruling pencils express the cubic quotient as a space of dimension at most eighteen, incompatible with the required twenty.

A smooth integral quintic point graph with disjoint isolated residual in a four-edge point-fiber finite Frobenius candidate must be elliptic with empty residual. In genus two the opposite contraction forces two alternating Weierstrass polarizations. Cyclic parity then forces three common commutators, giving an impossible complete intersection of degree eight supported on a sextic.

Every smooth elliptic quintic point graph in a finite Frobenius four-edge graph window has j=1728 and translation four-shift. Each projection center is an eigenline for one of two cyclic order-five groups. Each adjacent relation space is the entire mixed multiplication kernel. All four positions have the same order-five subgroup and adjacent translations do not differ by five-torsion. Two explicit reference embeddings and a finite list of torsion offsets reduce the candidates to finitely many one-parameter elliptic families. Sufficiency is open.

Only two explicitly specified indexed relation sequences can have smooth elliptic quintic point graphs: use either reference projection and alternate translation by the two branch points (1,0) and (-1,0). The full geometric cubic-overlap degeneracy calculation at 181 and a local lifting argument exclude all nontorsion shifts. The two signs cannot be indexed isomorphic if realized.

There are exactly two index-preserving isomorphism classes with point-fiber point graph a smooth integral quintic disjoint from the finite residual. Both are realized, the residual is empty, the two point graphs are reduced elliptic quintics, and their bare period is one. Each has five folded central quartics, with a four-parameter normalization certified by the degree-sixteen cutoff. The canonical four-shift is projectively the identity.

A finite Frobenius four-edge point-fiber graph cannot be a smooth integral rational quartic with disjoint finite residual. Seven mixed relations give a balanced quadratic syzygy bundle and a five-dimensional full cubic overlap. The required four-dimensional suboverlap would force a Hankel determinant simultaneously zero and nonzero. Smooth integral quartics with disjoint residual are elliptic with isolated length four.

Smooth plane cubic point graphs with disjoint finite residual are exactly all central PBW homogenizations of the three-dimensional smooth elliptic Sklyanin algebras with translation outside E[3]. This holds starting just with finite Frobenius and point fibers: consecutive pure relations rule out deficient transverse matrices, stability of the plane evaluation bundles gives cubic injectivity, and the ordinary central presentation follows. The residual is the length-eight affine critical scheme of an explicit cubic. All classes have bare period one.

For a twisted cubic point graph with disjoint finite residual, each six-point residual is scheme-isomorphic to a plane section of an explicit quadric and the three-by-three determinant. The cyclic tensor is the product of four binary edge diagonals and a four-qubit tensor. The canonical four-shift on the curve is either the identity or an involution: connected groups and all orders at least three are excluded.

The fixed ideal of the canonical shift on a reduced locally complete intersection curve is cut by a section of the dualizing sheaf times the squared polarization second difference. On any generically reduced normalized component the formula includes cotangent torsion and ramification. Smooth open-and-closed rational components are impossible. The full smooth curve plus disjoint finite residual stratum consists of the plane cubic, elliptic quartic, elliptic quintic, and bielliptic septic charts.

Every pure reduced point curve of degree at most three with disjoint finite residual is either a smooth plane cubic or a triangle. The full triangle stratum is the central PBW family over lambda in G_m minus one, with a split point and the quotient of P(1,1,1,2,2,2) by C3 squared over each lambda. All are AS, have period one, and are flat specializations of smooth cubic windows.

For every pure reduced quartic point graph with disjoint finite residual, the only possible singular curves are the two-conic nodal cycle and the spatial four-line cycle. Both have length-four residual and fixed-point-free canonical rotation with second difference of order at most two. Two explicit polygon coefficient charts have finite all-degree AS, isomorphism, and minimum-period tests, including all zero-coordinate strata.

All integral reduced quintic point graphs with disjoint finite residual in a standard AS window, including all singularities, are the two smooth elliptic quintics. The genus-two Gorenstein cubic separator yields a degree-three pencil and forces a double cover with incompatible fixed lengths. The non-Gorenstein cone vertex gives an Ore mark and a conic lift with pole degree at most two instead of three.

Classify all integral reduced septic point graphs including singularities by the same eight bielliptic coefficients: the sole condition is geometrically integral complete intersection. All such windows are AS, the original full isomorphism and period tests extend, and every singular window is a flat limit of the smooth five-dimensional moduli stratum. Every embedding-dimension-three point on any point-fiber graph is automatically a four-periodic Ore mark.

An integral reduced sextic point graph with disjoint finite residual can only be a singular canonical plane quartic of normalization genus zero or one, without finite residual. Nonplanar singularities, all hyperelliptic models and normalization genus two are excluded. Any nonidentity canonical four-shift is a plane homology of order two or four, with trivial squared polarization difference.

Exclude every singular integral sextic point graph with disjoint finite residual. The trisecant residual maps have degree one by the transpose degree-three correspondence and differential trace. Anti-invariant dualizing forms generate the plane involution function field; normalized ramification jets exclude identity, and cyclic eigensheaves exclude order four. Thus the entire reduced integral point-curve plus disjoint finite residual stratum is covered in degrees 3, 4, 5 and 7, including every singular integral model.

For an arbitrary one-dimensional point-fiber graph with pure hull Y the finite discrepancy has length 18-4d+2p_a(Y). Sextics are always pure of genus three with a (2,2) residual in each projection; quintic hulls have genus one or two. The conormal correction to the fixed length excludes embedded structure on every reduced integral hull of degree at least five, and excludes rational quartic hulls.

Every connected reduced pure open-and-closed curve in a point-fiber graph has positive arithmetic genus. In genus one it is smooth elliptic or a rational nodal polygon. Five-line polygons are impossible: two opposite contractions of the Frobenius tensor would fix every vertex, whereas the canonical shift is a fixed-point-free rotation. This closes every reduced genus-one quintic hull, leaving only the two smooth elliptic classes.

A line component gives a finite necessary and sufficient all-degree AS test: each opposite restriction along its shift orbit must have rank two. A conic component gives a mixed linear-quadratic syzygy test, also necessary and sufficient with embedded structures allowed. Their two-window atlases together with the two integral elliptic classes cover all quintic point graphs, reduced or not.

Every compatible plane cubic subscheme in a one-dimensional point-fiber graph, including nonreduced cubics or embedded intersections, forces a regular normal linear parameter. The entire window is a period-one central PBW lift of its ternary AS quotient. The two adjacent conormal presentations detect any failure of normality without smoothness or isolation.

The split and nonsplit double twisted cubics are impossible. For the nonsplit ribbon the Picard recurrence forces an ordinary unipotent shift and exact cyclic chart elimination contradicts embedding. No union of a twisted cubic and an integral quartic can be septic. All septic point graphs now have finite AS/isomorphism atlases; the only residual sextic support without established marks is two twisted cubics meeting in length four.

Exclude a sextic union of two twisted cubics for every length-four gluing. The cross-component degree-(1,1) correspondence determines its polarization, while an exchanging canonical involution forces the general trisecants into a smooth quadric even at nonreduced intersections. Thus all one-dimensional point-fiber graphs of degree at least four have finite AS/isomorphism atlases; among smaller degrees the only remaining unmarked hull is a twisted cubic with length-six defect.

For any full twisted-cubic point subgraph of a standard finite-Frobenius window with point fibers, every rank-two relation whose pencil has a basepoint gives a line module of Hilbert function n+1 with a principal first relation module, even before AS regularity. The expected Hilbert function in all windows is sufficient for Koszul two-sided AS regularity. A compatible pencil sequence ensures it, and the two secant determinant cubics each have a line factor or vanish identically.

Prove all-degree regularity on the residual twisted cubic whenever the auxiliary binary determinant is integral (including nodal and cuspidal curves), identically zero, or has a ruling fiber. Integral genus-one addition links sets of at most four secant pencils in every position. The only remaining auxiliary divisors are pairs of (1,1) graphs and doubled (1,1) graphs.

All doubled auxiliary (1,1) graphs on the residual twisted cubic are regular. The same holds for two inverse graph components at every position or a component with only involutive/identity transitions. In the entire residual cubic regime the secant schemes on both sides of every edge are isomorphic plane cubics; closed-set iteration decides the existence of a bilateral secant chain in finite time.

Finish all reduced split auxiliary binary determinants, including the two-node and tacnodal cases and mixed Moebius transitions. The nodal chart forces a common pair of coordinates and a common involution line of secants; the tacnodal chart forces the singular coordinate to agree everywhere. All one-dimensional point-fiber graphs now have finite all-degree regularity and indexed-isomorphism atlases, including the residual twisted cubic with its nonreduced finite structure.

For every finite point window of opposite rank eight with at least one simple local component, a middle support of dimension three certifies regularity; otherwise the two opposite pairs are simultaneously symmetrizable and the existing bisymmetric finite all-degree test is necessary and sufficient. The proof includes dependent commutators, nondiagonalizable commuting planes, and both skew alternatives.

Every finite rank-nine window with a simple local component and four-dimensional middle supports has at least one symmetric opposite pair. An irreducible four-plane in sl3 has at least three independent commutators. A rank-at-most-two generator of the remaining symmetric quadratic kernel certifies regularity. The open cases in this stratum reduce to rank-three or rank-four symmetric kernels.

For any finite point graph with an opposite symmetry and a smooth generator of its one-dimensional symmetric quadratic kernel, simultaneous surjectivity in one binary direction forces bisymmetry, including repeated eigenvalues. The only other alternative has exponential growth. The bisymmetric finite test therefore decides regularity throughout this stratum.

A rank-three symmetric kernel on a finite point graph forces either a bisymmetric window or exponential growth. In the full case a rank-two commutator with a cyclic operator determines the symmetric pairing even at repeated eigenvalues. In the deficient case binary septics produce exponentially many independent paths. At opposite rank nine with a simple local point the existence of a ternary middle support is now necessary and sufficient for regularity.

The mixed skew/symmetric marked chart is classified by a four-dimensional commutative Frobenius algebra with normalized functional and a projective nondegenerate ternary quadratic form. Regularity for all parameters, including nonreduced factors, is equivalent to nonisotropy of every lifted local socle in the matrix factor. Every finite point graph on this chart is regular, of opposite rank ten and minimal period two.

All finite one-opposite-symmetric windows of opposite rank at most nine admit a finite regularity decision without simple-point hypotheses. The whole regular mixed chart has rank ten and minimum period two. Its quartic Frobenius normal forms and residual groups are explicit, and finiteness is a ternary eigenvector test outside the noncurvilinear local algebra. Its eight-dimensional closure is a divisor in the nine-dimensional half-period component.

In every standard regular window the endpoint ranks of all nonzero cubic slices are at least two, without any symmetry, recurrence or finite-fiber assumption. Positive-dimensional fibers can therefore only be lines. A two-dimensional endpoint support determines at most one evaluation point, and a line on both sides forces both relation intersections to have dimension two.

In a standard regular window the centers of positive-dimensional projection fibers have dimension at most one on every edge. A curve of such centers sweeps out an irreducible surface in the next letter, and all but finitely many of its points also have predecessors. The surface bound allows singular cubics and does not assume absence of pure relations.

In every standard regular window each positive-dimensional component of the line-fiber center locus is itself a line. It sweeps a plane or a quadric. Nonlinear centers on a smooth quadric would be a conic or a twisted cubic, both excluded by a split path block or an endpoint overlap. Any three-dimensional edge projection gives the polynomial ring and the total divisor degree of any other edge projection is at most two.

Every moving line-fiber center sweeps a pencil in a plane, with the whole line of centers as the inverse fiber at the pencil vertex. Smooth quadrics force a separated arrow and cones force three consecutive-side pure relations with a common letter. The plane slice forces a nonzero pure relation on the opposite edge. Consequently pure-relation-free regular windows have only finitely many exceptional line fibers.

All bi-infinite birational chains of integral quadrics in regular windows extend to projective isomorphisms. In the absence of decomposable quadratic relations every surface projection belongs to the established polynomial, normal-plane, smooth-quadric or cone quotient classifications, including possible isolated exceptional fibers.

Every generically birational chain of surface components containing a plane is a chain of projective planes with linear transitions. A plane Koszul sheaf complex exact off finitely many points is exact everywhere. Consequently all regular windows with surface projections and only isolated exceptional line fibers belong to the established lists, even in the presence of pure relations.

No positive-dimensional family of line fibers occurs in a regular window. Any moving pencil would also move on the other side. Its three-letter block between independent centers gives a (2,2) determinant containing the diagonal. The resulting degree-two flat path schemes, including double diagonals, force exponential growth. This removes all fiber hypotheses from the coverage of windows with a surface projection.

At an isolated forward line fiber the reverse rank is two or three. The relations on the successor line form a square or rectangular binary pencil; any nonconstant generic successor is a complete rational normal linear system of degree at most three. Every two-sided center has a unique nonzero four-step self-block and has neighboring exceptional fibers cut out inside its intrinsic plane by binary quadratics.

A point can never have both a predecessor line and a successor line. Its hypothetical unique self-block extends over a two-dimensional first-order base of simultaneous rank-two deformations. Three scalar equations suffice to close two moving boundaries between fixed endpoints, giving a nonconstant infinitesimal loop and exponential growth.

With no surface projection, each forward branch center gives a unique finite chain of birational rational curves ending at a backward branch center, bijectively in a four-period window. Every successor on its birth line has that center as unique predecessor. The Pluecker degrees give exact zeroth and first moment identities for forward and backward defects; in particular any branching forces a periodic point sequence passing through a forward center.

Any residual branching window with no surface projection has at most twenty forward centers and a branching point orbit of period at most forty in each direction. Both a cyclic right and a cyclic left periodic point module have infinitely generated defining ideals, with exact first Tor dimensions. Within terminal recurrent components all forward defects of the same rational family concentrate at a single unramified parameter.

Exclude every exceptional line fiber in surface-free regular windows of opposite rank six or seven. At seven, opposite binary kernels would pair each forward center to a backward center by a conic of pure relations. The ensuing twisted cubic has a successor simultaneously contained in a plane and a quadric cone, contradicting the reversed degree. This covers all regular windows through opposite rank seven. A pure-free branching window must have opposite rank at least nine and a full L3 pencil.

Two moving lines between fixed centers force a nondegenerate ternary tensor on restriction and an opposite-rank lower bound 6+a+b-r. Without pure relations the bound is twelve, each center confines other successors to a canonical twisted cubic, and there are at most two centers per position. The two critical divisors of a two-line chain are secant or tangent intersections with those cubics.

At any simple finite point with full middle supports, one common marked triple span forces an opposite symmetry without assuming a bound on the opposite rank. The other span has dimension at most five. For distinct spans and bracket rank two it is exactly five, from complementary two-planes in a symplectic four-space. In particular no rank above ten has a common triple span at such a mark.

At a simple finite mark with full middle supports and common triple of cross-bracket rank two, the two commutators admit an invertible pencil member. A Sylvester equation reconstructs the common triple in terms of the pencil and three scalar parameters, subject to cyclicity and a trace condition.

When both marked spans have dimension four at a simple finite point with full middle supports, the common bracket rank is four or five. Both pairs admit simultaneous rank-one differences. At rank five each span has one commuting plane, and at rank four these planes form a pencil through a matrix of rank one modulo scalars.

In finite windows of opposite rank eight the two opposite marked slices have the same four-dimensional image at every point, including nonreduced components. A common-kernel line test on the other points and on marked tangent directions forces the induced identification to give an opposite symmetry on the whole scheme. Passing on both sides certifies the finite all-degree AS test without a simple point. Smooth determinantal cubics suffice on either side.

At an aligned finite mark the rank-one scheme in its four-dimensional matrix span has length at most four if finite. For length at most two the unique possible exceptional secant is rigid over Artin bases; at a curvilinear mark, or an embedding-dimension-two mark passing the tangent test, the induced map gives a scheme-wide opposite symmetry even with exceptional points elsewhere. A nonzero adjacent coordinate word has scheme support of length at least six.

All aligned finite marks with finite rank-one section of length at most two now force opposite symmetry, including planar local marks tangent to the exceptional secant. A curvilinear or simple mark with three distinct rank-one points also forces it, by separation on three noncoplanar lines.

Every positive-dimensional rank-one section of an aligned finite mark is a single reduced Segre ruling. Its unique common-kernel pencil has one fixed kernel direction over every Artin base. This forces opposite symmetry even at planar, nonreduced marks with exceptional tangent direction.

For an aligned finite slice with a length-three Gorenstein rank-one scheme, any simple or curvilinear mark forces opposite symmetry, including doubled and tripled directions. Every length-four rank-one section is Gorenstein and its algebra determines the entire slice as the trace multiplication form on its trace hyperplane.

The non-Gorenstein length-three rank-one slice has a two-by-two congruence normal form. For a simple or curvilinear mark its canonical length-six plane complete intersection forces opposite symmetry: otherwise all cofactors of a generically invertible plane matrix would be proportional. This covers all length-three slices at such marks.

For all finite Frobenius windows an opposite coordinate product has dimension exactly ten or sixteen. Any single mixed bilinear equation forces the two-step identification and opposite tensor symmetry. The criterion is independent of marks, opposite tensor rank and AS regularity and applies to arbitrary nonreduced point schemes.

For a reduced tetrahedral rank-one section at a simple or curvilinear finite mark, all six off-diagonal products in the two opposite coordinate systems coincide after a single unit normalization. Without opposite symmetry, their six alternating differences have disjoint supports of length one or two on the corresponding pairs of lines. The four diagonal corrections are quadratic and at least three are nonzero.

Pure-relation-free branching without a surface or a two-line corridor, in particular at opposite ranks 9 through 11, has exactly one forward and one backward center in each of two opposite positions. The only possible pairs of corridor lengths are (3,3),(3,7),(5,5). The degree-ten determinantal tangent obstruction excludes adjacent or isolated occupied positions.

Pure-relation-free branching without surfaces requires opposite rank at least eleven. Opposite forward and backward centers have successor and predecessor lines meeting at one point. Their marked row spaces meet in one rank-one matrix; at rank eleven their sum is the full perpendicular of the crossing point and the resulting quotient bundle has splitting (2,1,1).

Any branching window of opposite rank eight without surface projections has a forward or backward center with a two-dimensional middle support, even with pure relations. At rank nine, in the absence of such a center, every center has middle support three and the general point of its fiber line has middle support four. The primitive kernel degree bounds the loss in middle rank by local elementary divisors.

If the general successor of a curve-only branching center of middle support a has middle support four, the opposite rank is at least a+6. Two-line corridors require opposite rank at least nine. At opposite rank eight all centers have middle support two or four, and at most one forward center and one backward center occur per phase. Every forward center of middle support four has a preceding forward center of middle support two whose opposite annihilator is its successor line.

In a standard regular window of opposite rank eight with all projections at most one-dimensional, every fiber of each edge projection is empty or a point, including windows with pure relations. The last hypothetical configuration requires a three-dimensional annihilator of a space of biquadratics to contain a third-order jet and a decomposable tensor with a different right factor.

A common marked slice with four reduced rank-one vertices forces opposite symmetry on its row and column coordinate positions whenever the mark has tangent dimension at most one, even if all local factors are nonreduced. The projected kernel cross product is supported on at most four socles, and cubic separation and the absence of pure relations exclude every nonsymmetric case.

Every length-four rank-one common slice at a mark of tangent dimension at most one forces symmetry on its kernel-coordinate parity, for all length-four Gorenstein Artin types. Hence at opposite rank eight a finite window with such a mark either has an all-degree regular ternary contraction or is at least one-sided symmetric. The existing one-sided symmetric criterion therefore decides all-degree regularity throughout this stratum.

At opposite rank eight all-degree regularity is decidable for finite Frobenius windows with a planar mark whose maximal ideal has principal square. Thus the untested finite stratum has at most three closed points, each a nonstretched planar Gorenstein local ring of length at least six. The proof handles both types of length-three slices and all length-four slices at the mark.

The finite rank-eight all-degree regularity test covers a local factor of length six and therefore all windows on three or more closed points. Length-three rank-one slices give symmetry at arbitrary planar Cartier marks on an ordinary node or cusp. In any finite Frobenius window each coordinate line meets the point scheme in length at most three, without assuming a rank or reducedness.

A repeated linear factor in a finite cubic separator forces the alternating three-by-three space plus one symmetric rank-one matrix, with separator h times s squared. Three distinct plane factors force a short or positive-dimensional rank-one slice. At a single supporting point every length-four marked slice now gives opposite kernel symmetry even for arbitrary planar local rings. At two points the length-four curvilinear kernel discrepancy is excluded.

A two-line corridor requires opposite rank at least eleven even in the presence of pure relations. Both endpoint middle supports restrict surjectively to the opposite line, and every moving point on either line has middle support four. At rank eleven only endpoint supports three and a pure endpoint contraction of rank one are possible.

A plane meets any coordinate of a finite window in length at most seven. At opposite rank eight tangent incidence between two planar points is equivalent on opposite coordinates and cannot go in both directions at one position. In an untested two-support length-four slice the nonsymmetric kernel discrepancy must be supported at the mark itself and has length three curvilinear or length four of type (1,2,1), with a repeated-plane separator there.

If an untested finite rank-eight planar window has no local equations through degree three, it has a single support and a common length-eight subscheme on which all four coordinates are projectively identified. Each embedding is a complete intersection of three quadrics. Its ideal is the annihilator of the square of every tangent-plane equation. Consecutive tangent planes cut length six and each tangent plane cuts length seven.

A four-tensor whose four diagonal edge restrictions belong to the same complete-intersection net of quadrics splits into a bisymmetric tensor and a four-form. In the high-order finite rank-eight residual branch the common octad aligns the positions, and the common irreducible quadric forces the symmetric opposite block to have rank at least three. The four-form must vanish, contradicting the required nonsymmetric marked slice. Thus every still undecided planar mark has an equation of order two or three.

Every standard finite Frobenius window with finite edges and opposite rank eight has a finite all-degree Koszul and two-sided AS regularity decision. Middle support three certifies regularity. Otherwise one parity is symmetric, so the low-rank symmetric-kernel test and the bisymmetric finite test decide every candidate, including one- and two-support nonreduced schemes. The new argument applies once to the blowup of a multiplicity-two or -three plane carrier, including nonreduced carriers.

Finite-edge rank nine is regular exactly at a point of middle support three. In the single high-order chart a nonzero four-form requires opposite rank at least twelve. Together with surface and curve-graph coverage and branching exclusions, all windows through opposite rank eight have finite all-degree regularity and indexed-isomorphism tests. The sole residual rank-nine type has a pure relation and curve-only branching.

At every opposite rank a forward branching center of middle support two has a unique paired backward center in the preceding phase. Their binary support planes coincide and their two corresponding lines have generic middle support three. No other moving component in a finite branching corridor has generic middle support three: paired moving opposite annihilators would propagate backward past the starting center. At rank nine all centers have middle support two or three. Any consecutive string of nonlinear components contains at most one nonplanar curve; all planar components have degree at most three.

At opposite rank nine no curve-only branching is possible in a standard regular window, including windows with pure relations. A ternary center forces its second component to be a conic whose plane equation ends a pure relation. A binary center cannot have a forward center in the preceding phase. Ternary centers would then exist in all phases in both directions and force consecutive pure relations. Binary centers alone require adjacent nonplanar cubics, also impossible. This completes finite all-degree regularity and indexed-isomorphism recognition for every window of opposite rank at most nine.

In any finite-edge standard Frobenius window of full middle support, one planar local complete intersection whose two equations have order at least four forces bisymmetry at every opposite rank, whether or not residual support is present. Off the mark, linkage in two common unit coordinates identifies the same octad. Its net gives a half-turn on the point scheme, trivial on the entire large local factor by characteristic-zero tangent rigidity and hence globally by the support bound on adjacent words. Such windows cannot be regular at opposite rank above eight.

For any full-middle-support reduced finite twenty-point graph, two different marked four-spaces spanning a five-space force its Segre intersection to be positive-dimensional. A finite six-point intersection would have to supply at least thirteen secants. The square-coordinate dependency codes on those labeled secants recover the two hyperplanes up to a change on the missing edges, contradicting the distinct intersections even with two omitted pairs. A single quartic slice at a curvilinear mark already forces kernel-side symmetry without a common slice. Hence a spanning integral rank-one curve in the five-space forces symmetry.

For a reduced twenty-point finite window with full middle support, different marked four-spaces spanning a five-space force an opposite symmetry. A ruling cannot supply thirteen common-kernel pencils. For a plane conic the off-plane rank-one points and transverse contacts are controlled by one binary quadric. Projecting from its at most two distinguished points gives three independent opposite words supported on at most two points. The identically zero quadric yields a second conic or a symmetric matrix space. Consequently reduced finite rank ten has an opposite symmetry and reduced finite rank eleven is impossible under full middle support.

At rank ten, a four-middle-support branching center followed by a twisted cubic has exactly two forms for the restriction to its first line and second cubic, and forces a forward center on that cubic. The third curve has degree at most four. If nonplanar, it lies on a smooth quadric with projection degrees 1 and d3-1 and is followed by a moving plane curve through whose plane the original center passes, of degree at least d3-1. This excludes every (1,3,3,1) corridor with twisted cubic inner curves and either endpoint of full middle support.

At rank ten a four-support center followed by a second conic forces its unique first-line forward center to be ternary of singular pencil type. Its third curve and next position are planar; a cubic third curve has a backward center at its double point. Independently of rank, a singular ternary center identifies projected coordinates on the next pair. After a twisted cubic its third degree is between two and four (at most three if the projection center lies on the cubic), by the length-one bound for paths returning to their fixed start.

When no corridor consists of two lines, no binary forward or backward center can occur in any surface-free standard regular window. The paired binary equations place the moving curves of two phases on quadric cones. A forward center opposite the binary one would produce a twisted cubic through the vertex, forcing a backward center onto a line with unique predecessors. Without that opposite center the degree recurrence contradicts the degrees at both possible terminal centers. Consequently all moving components have full generic middle support, in particular for every remaining rank-ten branching candidate.

At rank ten a four-support forward center with a twisted cubic second curve reaches a center on that cubic whose successor line is the flat limit of the general pencil kernels and whose own second curve is a conic. The original third curve is a line or conic, a conic is followed by a line, and the second normal form forces a third line. Thus every four-support center reaches a ternary center within three edges, even in a terminal recurrent class.

Every full-middle-support branching center at rank ten has a second conic, never a twisted cubic. On either ruled kernel surface the true edge scheme is a divisor of bidegree (4,1). Frobenius orthogonality lifts a successor over each generic local factor including its multiplicity. The remaining successor minors have first bidegree at most three, hence vanish identically and would give a surface projection. Such a center is immediately followed on its first line by a singular ternary center.

At any rank without two-line corridors a twisted cubic second curve has generic residual matrix rank three: the other rank-two nets yield a (1,1) incidence scroll where the full edge divisor forces a surface projection or a second line. At rank ten the one remaining syzygy forces a third line and a quintic deficit. A line adjacent to a twisted cubic can only be the endpoint line on that side. Rank-ten branching therefore has either only conic second curves, with both orientations represented in every phase, or only (1,3,1) corridors with cyclic regular ternary endpoints, at most one per phase in each direction.

Every rank-ten standard regular window with all point projections of dimension at most one is unbranched. The cyclic regular ternary cubic option contradicts the square factor in its quintic deficit. In the all-conic configuration each phase has one forward and one backward center, and every corridor begins and ends with (1,2,1). A singular ternary center then annihilates its opposite forward center: its projected second conic and third line identify that point by its unique predecessor. The adjacent three-dimensional evaluation kernel forces the preceding center to have middle support at most two, already excluded. All remaining rank-ten recognition gaps therefore have four finite edges.

For a finite window of full middle support with eighteen simple points and one double point, opposite rank ten forces an opposite symmetry and rank eleven is impossible. Weighted residual pencils exclude rulings; a conic with an embedded tangent cannot supply twelve distinct pencils, while two detached nodes give symmetry even over dual numbers. For a reduced six-node section the thirteen edge stresses force coincidence at the unique double point. Re-marking there combines nine simple marks in one parity into a common four-space.

At a simple five-space mark of any curvilinear finite graph with full middle support, projected evaluation valuations exclude every ruling. Six reduced nodes force a secant collision at a nonsimple graph point, and a conic with two detached reduced nodes forces symmetry. For seventeen simple points and one curvilinear triple point, opposite rank ten forces symmetry and rank eleven is impossible.

A finite full-middle-support graph on at least eighteen geometric sites forces opposite symmetry at opposite rank ten and excludes rank eleven. For two double points, two first jets in a confluent six-node square configuration force a forbidden secant equality. Each conic with an embedded node puts the simple mark on the fixed line through both double points, leaving at most one exceptional mark per parity. In a reduced six-node slice every nonsimple graph point has proportional contractions.

In the marked one-sided symmetric finite branch with symmetric nets spanning a four-space, the determinant of the prescribed commutator is the product of the linear commutator of their common plane and the conic of their trace normal. It vanishes identically exactly when the common plane commutes. For three independent target brackets and either four- or five-dimensional sum, every irreducible realizing triple is reconstructed on sixteen cyclic charts from one traceless matrix satisfying two linear and two quadratic trace equations and linear consistency conditions.

Finite curvilinear graphs on seventeen sites with full middle support force symmetry at opposite rank ten. Rank eleven is excluded there as well: four shared finite marks force all three double points into a common plane, leaving no room for any opposite exceptional mark. An embedded conic pencil charges the double weight of a fixed kernel line, forcing each exceptional mark onto the secant of a length-two scheme supported on nonsimple graph points. At a confluent six-node slice the relative first-jet speed on both hyperplane cuts is identical.

On every finite full-middle-support graph with at least seventeen geometric sites, opposite rank ten forces an opposite symmetry and rank eleven is impossible. At a planar Gorenstein length-four site, embedded conic pencils select one of two isotropic tangent directions. The only loss in the projected ruling bound is a socle contact, which produces rulings with the same tangent-plane factor in both re-marked four-spaces; the two-space incidence count then excludes it globally.

Three independent commutators of an irreducible traceless three-plane of 3-by-3 matrices cannot all send one fixed plane to one fixed line. Both the transverse and incident line cases force reducibility or a common self-adjoint form with only two independent compressed skew brackets. In every marked one-sided symmetric finite branch with unequal symmetric nets and three independent brackets the cubic determinant is nonzero. In particular the common plane of two symmetric nets with four-dimensional sum cannot commute.

For a pencil containing an invertible prescribed commutator, the four-coefficient linear reconstruction has rank three or four. A singular defect direction is a multiple determinantal root. All invertible defect directions give line components of an explicit conic of the target three-space and admit an exact square-root and affine-line reconstruction using two Sylvester inverses, including nondiagonalizable matrices.

The linear reconstruction has full rank four in a general direction except exactly for one explicit transverse block form with a nonsymmetric invertible two-by-two matrix. This form has a triple-line determinant and a square-zero planar triple rank-one slice. It cannot occur in any finite window of the unequal symmetric-net branch. A length-four Veronese section in a triple line forces a common eigenvector and hence an entire line over one adjacent point. The generic-direction linear reconstruction therefore always has full rank in this finite branch. A nine-word determinant equals minus the cube of the original commutator determinant.

For every prescribed projective trace normal N and line ell, including every nilpotent/Jordan type and repeated or tangent factor, there is a nineteen-dimensional irreducible marked chart whose geometric generic window is finite, opposite rank ten, quadratic Koszul and left/right AS regular, and whose mixed discriminant is ell times v-transpose N v. The rank-one determinantal cone of two by three matrices describes the marked local incidence. Through the split tetrahedron the class image for each fixed cubic has dimension six, trivial generic projective automorphisms and generic minimum period four. For every irreducible symmetric three-plane with independent self-brackets, all complementary three-planes of each prescribed cubic are reconstructed by two scalar equations and linear algebra, including singular/reducible cubics and nonreduced harmonic base schemes. The zero center is scheme-theoretically the distinguished plane plus that length-four base. Outside the exception a two-dimensional family of apolar reduced frames yields an eight-dimensional indexed-class image of finite rank-ten geometric-generic AS windows with that precise cubic. Inside the exception every apolar length-four divisor contains a length-three divisor giving a commuting plane, even with nonreduced support. A smooth exceptional cubic with nonsingular metric is computed explicitly.

For an irreducible symmetric first net with dependent self-brackets, every smooth prescribed cubic through its harmonic base has a complete rational conic of complementary symmetric planes. Together with the elliptic quintic for independent self-brackets, this handles the complementary-plane step for every irreducible first net over smooth cubics, including the fixed-metric exceptions.

All ordered traceless triples with smooth commutator determinant are recovered through a six-dimensional linear space over auxiliary determinantal representations of the same cubic. The exact inverse of the three-commutator map on every fixed ordered traceless target with smooth determinant is four symmetric 3x3 adjugate equations.
